fixed_tail_proof.multinomial: mN=omegaN(phi)=OP1. On |mN|<=K, for R>=K and largeN, conditional Lindeberg is bounded by4 omegaN(phi²1{|phi|>R}). Fixed-R LLN and then target L2 tail limit prove convergence in probability.

def-smc-clt-function-classes-and-varianc.Definition:
Fix a finite horizon $T$. At each $0\le t\le T$, let $\pi_t$ be a probability law on a measurable particle space $\Theta_t$. Let $\widetilde\pi_0$ be an initial proposal with $\pi_0\ll\widetilde\pi_0$, and fix $\upsilon_0=d\pi_0/d\widetilde\pi_0$. For $1\le t\le T$, let $k_t$ be a probability kernel from $\Theta_{t-1}$ to $\Theta_t$, and put
$$\widetilde\pi_t(A)=\int_{\Theta_{t-1}}k_t(x,A)\,\pi_{t-1}(dx).$$
Assume $\pi_t\ll\widetilde\pi_t$ and fix a nonnegative Radon–Nikodym version $\upsilon_t=d\pi_t/d\widetilde\pi_t$, so $\widetilde\pi_t(\upsilon_t)=1$. The BCS-41 sequential importance-resampling algorithm [[alg-sequential-importance-resampling]] is this scheme on path spaces when $k_t$ appends a proposal transition. Under the support and measurable versions of [[thm-feynman-kac-path-radon-nikodym-weight]], its normalized incremental weight is $\upsilon_t=(Z_{t-1}/Z_t)G_t r_t$ for $t\ge1$, and $\upsilon_0=G_0\rho_0/Z_0$ initially. The previous normalized target is already part of $\widetilde\pi_t$; one does not multiply by the full earlier path-weight product again.

For a measurable vector function $\phi:\Theta_t\to\mathbb R^d$, write $\mu(\phi)=\int\phi\,d\mu$ and
$$\operatorname{Cov}_{\mu}(\phi)=\int(\phi-\mu(\phi))(\phi-\mu(\phi))^\top\,d\mu,$$
when the second moment is finite. Also write $k_t\phi(x)=\int\phi(z)k_t(x,dz)$ and
$$\operatorname{Cov}_{k_t}(\phi)(x)=\int(\phi(z)-k_t\phi(x))(\phi(z)-k_t\phi(x))^\top k_t(x,dz).$$

The source recursive test classes are
$$\Phi_0^{(d)}=\{\phi:\widetilde\pi_0(\|\phi\|^2)<\infty\},$$
and, for $t\ge1$,
$$\Phi_t^{(d)}=\left\{\phi:\text{ for some }\delta>0,\ \widetilde\pi_t(\|\upsilon_t\phi\|^{2+\delta})<\infty\ \text{ and }\ x\mapsto k_t(\upsilon_t\phi)(x)\in\Phi_{t-1}^{(d)}\right\}.$$
Assume $1\in\Phi_t^{(1)}$ for every $t$. This is the source theorem's explicit normalizing-weight condition. For the recursive post-resampling CLTs proved on this page, use the stronger classes $\Psi_t^{(d)}$. At $t=0$, let $\Psi_0^{(d)}$ consist of the $\phi\in\Phi_0^{(d)}$ for which $\widetilde\pi_0(\|\upsilon_0(\phi-\pi_0(\phi))\|^2)<\infty$ and $\pi_0(\|\phi\|^2)<\infty$. The initial normalizing denominator needs only its finite first moment $\widetilde\pi_0(\upsilon_0)=1$. For $t\ge1$, let $\Psi_t^{(d)}$ consist of the $\phi\in\Phi_t^{(d)}$ for which $\pi_t(\|\phi\|^2)<\infty$ and $x\mapsto E_t(\phi-\pi_t(\phi))(x)\in\Psi_{t-1}^{(d)}$. Here $E_t h=k_t(\upsilon_t h)$ is the operator defined below. Only target second moments are required: fixed-tail truncation supplies the conditional selection Lindeberg condition without a target higher-moment assumption. The recursive target moments supply the offspring variance at every earlier selection used in the induction. The source $\Phi_t$ conditions alone need not imply them. The source condition $1\in\Phi_t$ and these recursive target moments are the stated hypotheses for the CLT induction; no higher initial normalizer moment is required.

Define the mutation covariance operators recursively. At time zero,
$$\widetilde V_0(\phi)=\operatorname{Cov}_{\widetilde\pi_0}(\phi).$$
For $t\ge1$,
$$\widetilde V_t(\phi)=\widehat V_{t-1}(k_t\phi)+\int\operatorname{Cov}_{k_t}(\phi)(x)\,\pi_{t-1}(dx).$$
The weighted-estimator covariance is
$$V_t(\phi)=\widetilde V_t\!\left(\upsilon_t(\phi-\pi_t(\phi))\right).$$
For a measurable vector function $h$ on $\Theta_t$, define the forward operator from $\Theta_{t-1}$ by
$$E_t h(x)=k_t(\upsilon_t h)(x)=\int\upsilon_t(z)h(z)\,k_t(x,dz).$$
For $k<t$, write $E_{k+1:t}=E_{k+1}\circ\cdots\circ E_t$; set $E_{t+1:t}$ to the identity operator.
For multinomial offspring resampling set
$$\widehat V_t^{\mathrm{multi}}(\phi)=V_t(\phi)+\operatorname{Cov}_{\pi_t}(\phi).$$
For residual offspring resampling, let $r(u)=u-\lfloor u\rfloor$. When $c_t=\widetilde\pi_t(r(\upsilon_t))>0$, define the formal source candidate
$$R_t^{\mathrm{cand}}(\phi)=\widetilde\pi_t\!\left(r(\upsilon_t)\phi\phi^\top\right)-\frac{\widetilde\pi_t(r(\upsilon_t)\phi)\,\widetilde\pi_t(r(\upsilon_t)\phi)^\top}{c_t}.$$
Set $R_t=R_t^{\mathrm{cand}}$ and $\widehat V_t^{\mathrm{res}}=V_t+R_t$ only when $\widetilde\pi_t(\upsilon_t\in\{1,2,\ldots\})=0$; then $c_t>0$ and the finite-sample floor discontinuities are avoided. If $\upsilon_t=1$ $\widetilde\pi_t$-almost everywhere, all normalized weights are exactly equal and residual offspring are deterministic; in that special case put $R_t=0$. No residual covariance is assigned when $c_t=0$ but $\upsilon_t$ is not almost everywhere one: the finite-sample normalization can move positive integer weights across floor boundaries. The B-page counterexamples show why the general positive-integer-atom branch remains unassigned.
def-smc-clt-function-classes-and-varianc.Remarks:
The classes and recursions are definitions. The fixed-horizon CLT proofs below establish finiteness where their stated hypotheses apply. In particular, the source class $\Phi_t^{(d)}$ alone does not ensure $\operatorname{Cov}_{\pi_t}(\phi)<\infty$; the recursive target-moment class $\Psi_t^{(d)}$ is used for the stated post-resampling conclusions. The residual formula requires a separate continuity condition at positive integer weights; the B-page records finite-state failures without it. For an arbitrary weighted initial proposal, the source class $\Phi_0=L^2(\widetilde\pi_0)$ is not by itself enough: the displayed initial weighted-numerator and target moments in $\Psi_0$ are imposed explicitly.

The stronger $\Psi$ hypotheses retain both locally proved fixed-horizon outputs, not the false claim that every source-$\Phi$ test has finite post-selection covariance. Separately, a weighted-only initial ratio CLT needs only a target-integrable test and its centered weighted numerator in $L^2(\widetilde\pi_0)$; its denominator still needs only $\widetilde\pi_0(\upsilon_0)=1$.

lem-smc-multinomial-resampling-clt.Statement:
Fix a time $t$ in the finite-horizon SIR system of [[def-smc-clt-function-classes-and-variance-recursions]]. Let $\omega_t^N$ be its corrected weighted empirical law and let $\check\eta_t^N$ be the empirical law after multinomial offspring resampling. Suppose $\pi_t(\phi^2)<\infty$, the empirical-law conclusions of [[lem-smc-finite-horizon-empirical-law]] hold, and
$$\sqrt N\{\omega_t^N(\phi)-\pi_t(\phi)\}\Rightarrow N(0,V)$$
for a finite $V\ge0$. Then
$$\sqrt N\{\check\eta_t^N(\phi)-\omega_t^N(\phi)\}\Rightarrow N(0,\operatorname{Var}_{\pi_t}(\phi)),$$
asymptotically independently of the weighted-estimator fluctuation, and
$$\sqrt N\{\check\eta_t^N(\phi)-\pi_t(\phi)\}\Rightarrow N\!\left(0,V+\operatorname{Var}_{\pi_t}(\phi)\right).$$
lem-smc-multinomial-resampling-clt.Facts & Assumptions:
**Given:** The corrected weighted empirical law, the multinomial selection rule, the target second-moment condition $\pi_t(\phi^2)<\infty$, and the weighted-estimator CLT in the Statement.

[A1] [[def-axiom-of-choice]]: AC is inherited through the finite-horizon particle-law construction and the cited probability limit theorem.

[F1] [[def-smc-clt-function-classes-and-variance-recursions]]: the target variance is $\pi_t((\phi-\pi_t\phi)^2)$ for a target-square-integrable test. The Statement assumes this second-moment domain.

[F2] [[alg-multinomial-and-residual-offspring-resampling]]: Conditional on the corrected particles, multinomial offspring are IID draws from $\omega_t^N$.

[F3] [[lem-smc-finite-horizon-empirical-law]]: For every $\pi_t$-integrable test $h$, $\omega_t^N(h)\to\pi_t(h)$ in probability.

[F4] [[thm-lindeberg-feller-central-limit-theorem-sufficiency]]: A centered independent triangular array with positive total variance and the Lindeberg condition, divided by its row standard deviation, converges to $N(0,1)$.

[F5] [[cor-chebyshev-inequality-for-random-variables]]: For a square-integrable variable on any probability space, the probability of an absolute centered deviation at least $a>0$ is at most its variance divided by $a^2$.

[F6] [[thm-slutsky-for-real-random-variables]]: Multiplying a distributionally convergent real variable by one converging in probability to a constant gives the scaled limit.
lem-smc-multinomial-resampling-clt.Proof:
**Given:** The hypotheses in the Statement.

1.1 Let $\mathcal F_N$ contain the corrected particles and their weights. By [F2], conditionally on $\mathcal F_N$ the selected values $Y_1^N,\ldots,Y_N^N$ are IID with law $\omega_t^N$. Their centered conditional variance is $s_N^2=\omega_t^N(\phi^2)-\omega_t^N(\phi)^2$, which converges in probability to $s^2=\operatorname{Var}_{\pi_t}(\phi)$ by [F1] and [F3]. [A1, F1, F2, F3, given]

1.2 Put $m_N=\omega_t^N(\phi)$ and $\xi_i^N=\phi(Y_i^N)-m_N$. By [F3], $m_N\to\pi_t\phi$ in probability, hence $m_N=O_P(1)$. For a fixed threshold $a>0$, choose fixed $K$ and then $R\ge K$. On $\{|m_N|\le K\}$ and for all sufficiently large $N$ with $a\sqrt N>R+K$, the event $|\phi(Y_i^N)-m_N|>a\sqrt N$ implies $|\phi(Y_i^N)|>R$, and $|\phi(Y_i^N)-m_N|^2\le4\phi(Y_i^N)^2$ there. Thus the conditional Lindeberg sum is at most $4\omega_t^N(\phi^2\mathbf1_{\{|\phi|>R\}})$ on that event. For fixed $R$, [F3] makes this upper bound converge to $4\pi_t(\phi^2\mathbf1_{\{|\phi|>R\}})$, which tends to zero as $R\to\infty$ by the finite target second moment. Given any error probability, first choose $K$ so that the probability of $|m_N|>K$ is small, then choose $R\ge K$ with this tail integral small, and finally let $N\to\infty$. This proves that the conditional Lindeberg sum tends to zero in probability using only target $L^2$. [F1, F2, F3, step 1.1, given, algebra]

2.1 Along any subsequence, choose a further subsequence on which $s_N\to s$ almost surely. If $s>0$, then eventually $s_N>s/2$; the normalized Lindeberg sum for draws divided by $s_N\sqrt N$ is bounded by step 1.2 at threshold $as/2$, divided by $s_N^2$. It therefore tends to zero in probability, and a further subsequence makes that convergence almost sure. Apply [F4] to obtain a standard-normal limit for the normalized row. Slutsky [F6] with $s_N\to s$ gives convergence of the conditional characteristic function of $N^{-1/2}\sum_i\xi_i^N$ to $e^{-u^2s^2/2}$. If $s=0$, conditional [F5] gives $P(|N^{-1/2}\sum_i\xi_i^N|>a\mid\mathcal F_N)\le\min(1,s_N^2/a^2)\to0$, giving the degenerate characteristic-function limit. The subsequence criterion therefore gives convergence in probability of these conditional characteristic functions along the full sequence. [F4, F5, F6, step 1.1, step 1.2]

2.2 The conditional characteristic functions are bounded by one, so their differences from $e^{-u^2s^2/2}$ converge to zero in $L^1$. For arbitrary real $v,u$, multiply the conditional resampling characteristic function at $u$ by the bounded factor $e^{iv\sqrt N(\omega_t^N(\phi)-\pi_t(\phi))}$ and take expectations. The resulting joint characteristic function tends to $e^{-v^2V/2}e^{-u^2s^2/2}$. Thus the resampling fluctuation is asymptotically independent of the weighted fluctuation, and their sum has variance $V+s^2$. [step 2.1, given, algebra] ∎

lem-smc-residual-resampling-clt-away-fro.Statement:
Fix a time $t$ in the finite-horizon SIR system of [[def-smc-clt-function-classes-and-variance-recursions]]. Let $X_t^{1:N}$ have proposal empirical law $\eta_t^N$, corrected law $\omega_t^N$, and residual-resampled law $\check\eta_t^N$. Assume the proposal empirical law converges in probability for every integrable test as in [[lem-smc-finite-horizon-empirical-law]], the weighted estimate has a finite-variance CLT
$$\sqrt N\{\omega_t^N(\phi)-\pi_t(\phi)\}\Rightarrow N(0,V),$$
and $\pi_t(\phi^2)<\infty$. Write $u=\upsilon_t$ and assume either $u=1$ $\widetilde\pi_t$-almost everywhere, or
$$\widetilde\pi_t(u\in\{1,2,\ldots\})=0.$$
In the second case $c=\widetilde\pi_t(r(u))>0$. Then, with
$$R_t(\phi)=\widetilde\pi_t(r(u)\phi^2)-\frac{\widetilde\pi_t(r(u)\phi)^2}{c},$$
where $R_t(\phi)=0$ in the constant-weight case,
$$\sqrt N\{\check\eta_t^N(\phi)-\omega_t^N(\phi)\}\Rightarrow N(0,R_t(\phi)),$$
asymptotically independently of the weighted-estimator fluctuation, and
$$\sqrt N\{\check\eta_t^N(\phi)-\pi_t(\phi)\}\Rightarrow N(0,V+R_t(\phi)).$$
lem-smc-residual-resampling-clt-away-fro.Facts & Assumptions:
**Given:** The proposal empirical-law convergence, the weighted-estimator CLT, the target second-moment condition, and the residual offspring algorithm in the Statement.

[A1] [[def-axiom-of-choice]]: AC is inherited through the finite-horizon particle-law construction and the cited probability limit theorem.

[F1] [[def-smc-clt-function-classes-and-variance-recursions]]: $u=d\pi_t/d\widetilde\pi_t$, $\widetilde\pi_t(u)=1$, $r(v)=v-\lfloor v\rfloor$, and the formal residual candidate is assigned as $R_t$ only in the no-positive-integer-atom branch or the constant-weight branch.

[F2] [[alg-multinomial-and-residual-offspring-resampling]]: For normalized weights $\rho_i$, residual resampling gives each particle $\lfloor N\rho_i\rfloor$ deterministic copies and fills the remaining count with IID draws proportional to $r(N\rho_i)$.

[F3] [[lem-smc-finite-horizon-empirical-law]]: The proposal and corrected empirical laws converge in probability for integrable tests.

[F4] [[thm-lindeberg-feller-central-limit-theorem-sufficiency]]: A centered independent triangular array with positive total variance and the Lindeberg condition, divided by its row standard deviation, converges to $N(0,1)$.

[F5] [[cor-chebyshev-inequality-for-random-variables]]: For a square-integrable variable on any probability space, the probability of an absolute centered deviation at least $a>0$ is at most its variance divided by $a^2$.

[F6] [[thm-slutsky-for-real-random-variables]]: Multiplying a distributionally convergent real variable by one converging in probability to a constant gives the scaled limit.
lem-smc-residual-resampling-clt-away-fro.Proof:
**Given:** The hypotheses in the Statement.

1.1 Put $\bar u_N=\eta_t^N(u)$ and $b_i^N=r(u(X_t^i)/\bar u_N)$ on the event $\bar u_N>0$, whose probability tends to one by [F3]. If $u=1$ almost everywhere, every finite normalized weight is $1/N$ and residual selection is deterministic, so the resampling fluctuation is zero. In the other case, for the three tests $a=1,\phi,\phi^2$, where $\pi_t(\phi^2)<\infty$, one has
$$\frac1N\sum_i b_i^Na(X_t^i)\xrightarrow{P}\widetilde\pi_t(r(u)a).$$
To verify this triangular empirical limit, fix $M$ and first restrict to $u\le M$ and $|\phi|\le M$. The compact $u$ interval meets only finitely many positive-integer discontinuities of $r$. Delete open $\gamma$-neighborhoods of those integers. On the remaining compact set, $r(u/\bar u_N)\to r(u)$ uniformly as $\bar u_N\to1$, and $|a|\le \max(1,M,M^2)$, so [F3] gives convergence of the restricted averages. Each deleted neighborhood has proposal integral of $|a|$ tending to zero as $\gamma\downarrow0$: it lies where $u\ge1/2$, and $\widetilde\pi_t(u|a|)=\pi_t(|a|)<\infty$; the no-atom condition gives the limit zero. [F3] controls its empirical average for each fixed $\gamma$. For the tails, when $\bar u_N\in[1/2,2]$, $b_i^N\le2u(X_t^i)$; hence the $|\phi|>M$ contribution is bounded by $2\eta_t^N(u|a|\mathbf1_{\{|\phi|>M\}})$, whose limit tends to zero by target integrability. On $u>M$, use $b_i^N\le1$ and $\widetilde\pi_t(|a|\mathbf1_{\{u>M\}})\le M^{-1}\pi_t(|a|)$, with [F3] again controlling the empirical average. The corresponding target tails obey the same bounds because $r(u)\le u$ and $r(u)\le1$. Taking first $N\to\infty$, then $\gamma\downarrow0$ and $M\to\infty$, proves the claim. [F1, F3, given, algebra]

1.2 Taking $a=1$ in step 1.1 gives $N^{-1}\sum_i b_i^N\to c$. Here $c>0$: if $c=0$, then $u$ is integer-valued almost surely; the no-positive-integer-atom assumption would force $u=0$ almost surely, contradicting $\widetilde\pi_t(u)=1$. Thus the number $M_N=\sum_i b_i^N$ of residual draws diverges and $M_N/N\to c$. Their conditional sampling probabilities are $b_i^N/M_N$. [F1, F2, step 1.1, algebra]

2.1 Let $m_N=M_N^{-1}\sum_i b_i^N\phi(X_t^i)$. Given the particles, the residual offspring contribution to the centered, $\sqrt N$-scaled empirical mean is $N^{-1/2}\sum_{\ell=1}^{M_N}(\phi(Y_\ell^N)-m_N)$, with IID conditional draws $Y_\ell^N$ from probabilities $b_i^N/M_N$. By step 1.1 its conditional variance converges in probability to
$$c\left\{\frac{\widetilde\pi_t(r(u)\phi^2)}c-\left(\frac{\widetilde\pi_t(r(u)\phi)}c\right)^2\right\}=R_t(\phi).$$
The residual draw mean $m_N$ is bounded in probability by the $a=\phi$ limit in step 1.1 and $M_N/N\to c>0$. Fix a threshold $a_0>0$ and fixed $K$, then $R\ge K$. On $\{|m_N|\le K,\ \bar u_N\in[1/2,2]\}$, for sufficiently large $N$ with $a_0\sqrt N>R+K$, the conditional Lindeberg sum for $N^{-1/2}\sum_{\ell=1}^{M_N}(\phi(Y_\ell^N)-m_N)$ is at most $4N^{-1}\sum_i b_i^N\phi(X_t^i)^2\mathbf1_{\{|\phi(X_t^i)|>R\}}$. Since $b_i^N\le2u(X_t^i)$ on this event, it is at most $8\eta_t^N(u\phi^2\mathbf1_{\{|\phi|>R\}})$. For fixed $R$, [F3] makes this converge to $8\widetilde\pi_t(u\phi^2\mathbf1_{\{|\phi|>R\}})=8\pi_t(\phi^2\mathbf1_{\{|\phi|>R\}})$, which tends to zero as $R\to\infty$. Choosing $K$, then $R$, then $N$ controls the exceptional mean event and the integrable fixed tail; $\bar u_N\to1$ handles the normalization event. Thus conditional Lindeberg holds under target $L^2$, with no target higher moment. [F1, F2, F3, F4, step 1.1, step 1.2, given, algebra]

2.2 Along any subsequence, choose a further subsequence on which the conditional residual variance converges almost surely. If $R_t(\phi)>0$, the conditional standard deviation is eventually greater than $\sqrt{R_t(\phi)}/2$. Apply the bound in step 2.1 at threshold $a\sqrt{R_t(\phi)}/2$ and divide by the conditional variance; this gives the Lindeberg condition after normalizing the residual sum by its conditional standard deviation. Conditional [F4] gives a standard-normal limit, and Slutsky [F6] with the conditional standard deviation converging to $\sqrt{R_t(\phi)}$ gives the characteristic-function limit $e^{-u_0^2R_t(\phi)/2}$. If $R_t(\phi)=0$, conditional [F5] bounds the deviation probability by the conditional variance divided by the squared threshold, giving the same degenerate limit. AC is inherited only through the particle law and conditional CLT supplier [F4]; the finite residual calculation adds no choice. The subsequence criterion gives convergence in probability along the full sequence. These conditional characteristic functions are bounded by one. For arbitrary real $v,u_0$, multiply this conditional characteristic function at $u_0$ by $e^{iv\sqrt N(\omega_t^N(\phi)-\pi_t(\phi))}$ and integrate. The limit is $e^{-v^2V/2}e^{-u_0^2R_t(\phi)/2}$, proving joint asymptotic independence and adding $R_t(\phi)$ to $V$. The deterministic-floor part is centered at its conditional expectation, so the conditional mean of the selected empirical law is exactly $\omega_t^N(\phi)$. [A1, F2, F4, F5, F6, given, step 2.1, algebra] ∎

lem-smc-mutation-and-weighted-correction.Statement:
Fix $t\ge1$. Suppose the selected empirical array at time $t-1$ has the CLT with covariance $\widehat V_{t-1}$ for $k_t\psi$. Let $\psi:\Theta_t\to\mathbb R$ satisfy $\widetilde\pi_t(|\psi|^{2+\delta})<\infty$ for some $\delta>0$ and $k_t\psi\in\Phi_{t-1}^{(1)}$. Then the proposal empirical mean after mutation satisfies
$$\sqrt N\left(\eta_t^N(\psi)-\widetilde\pi_t(\psi)\right)\Rightarrow N\!\left(0,\widehat V_{t-1}(k_t\psi)+\pi_{t-1}\!\left(\operatorname{Var}_{k_t}(\psi)\right)\right)=N(0,\widetilde V_t(\psi)).$$
For weighted correction, take $\psi=\upsilon_t(\phi-\pi_t(\phi))$ and explicitly require the preceding selected-population CLT for $k_t\psi=E_t(\phi-\pi_t(\phi))$. In particular, if $\phi\in\Psi_t^{(1)}$, $1\in\Phi_s^{(1)}$ for $0\le s\le t$, and this preceding selected CLT holds, the weighted corrected estimate satisfies
$$\sqrt N\left(\omega_t^N(\phi)-\pi_t(\phi)\right)\Rightarrow N(0,V_t(\phi)).$$
At $t=0$, a separate weighted-only conclusion holds whenever $\pi_0(|\phi|)<\infty$ and $Z=\upsilon_0(\phi-\pi_0\phi)\in L^2(\widetilde\pi_0)$: the weighted estimate has the ratio CLT with variance $V_0(\phi)=\widetilde\pi_0(Z^2)$. No target second moment, proposal second moment of $\phi$, or denominator second moment is required for this weighted-only conclusion. The stronger $\Psi_0$ assumptions imply it and support subsequent selected-population conclusions.
lem-smc-mutation-and-weighted-correction.Facts & Assumptions:
**Given:** The finite-horizon particle scheme, the previous selected-population CLT, and the function-class hypotheses in the Statement.

[A1] [[def-axiom-of-choice]]: AC is inherited through the finite-horizon particle-law construction and the Lindeberg–Feller supplier.

[F1] [[def-smc-clt-function-classes-and-variance-recursions]]: $\widetilde\pi_t=\pi_{t-1}k_t$, $\pi_t=\upsilon_t\widetilde\pi_t$, and $\Psi_t$ supplies a target second moment and recursive membership of $k_t(\upsilon_t(\phi-\pi_t\phi))$ in $\Psi_{t-1}$.

[F2] [[alg-sequential-importance-resampling]]: Conditional on the selected parents, the next proposal particles are drawn independently through $k_t$ and are then corrected by the incremental RN weights.

[F3] [[lem-smc-finite-horizon-empirical-law]]: Integrable proposal and selected empirical averages converge in probability to their target-law integrals at each fixed time.

[F4] [[thm-lindeberg-feller-central-limit-theorem-sufficiency]]: A centered independent triangular array with positive total variance and the Lindeberg condition, divided by its row standard deviation, converges to $N(0,1)$.

[F5] [[thm-slutsky-for-real-random-variables]]: If $X_N\Rightarrow X$ and $Y_N\to c$ in probability, then $X_NY_N\Rightarrow cX$; for $c\ne0$, the corresponding ratio converges to $X/c$.

[F6] [[cor-chebyshev-inequality-for-random-variables]]: For a square-integrable variable on any probability space, the probability of an absolute centered deviation at least $a>0$ is at most its variance divided by $a^2$.

[F7] [[thm-dominated-convergence]]: integrable domination permits passage to limits under the integral.
lem-smc-mutation-and-weighted-correction.Proof:
**Given:** The hypotheses in the Statement.

1.1 At $t=0$, the centered weighted numerator $Z=\upsilon_0(\phi-\pi_0\phi)$ has mean zero and finite second moment under the weighted-only assumptions; the $\Psi_0$ assumptions are sufficient for them. If its variance $\sigma_Z^2$ is positive, its IID row satisfies Lindeberg because $\sigma_Z^{-2}E[Z^2\mathbf1_{\{|Z|>a\sigma_Z\sqrt N\}}]\to0$ by [F7] for each $a>0$. Thus [F4] gives the IID CLT; if its variance is zero, [F6] gives convergence of its centered sample mean to zero. The denominator $\eta_0^N(\upsilon_0)$ converges to one by [F3], since $\widetilde\pi_0(\upsilon_0)=1$. Slutsky [F5] gives the ratio CLT with variance $V_0(\phi)$. For $t\ge1$, $\Phi_t$ is closed under finite linear combinations: use the smaller moment exponent, the $L^p$ triangle inequality, and linearity of kernel integration. The same arguments together with the target-moment condition show closure of $\Psi_t$. If $\phi\in\Psi_t$, then $\psi=\upsilon_t(\phi-\pi_t\phi)$ has a finite proposal $2+\delta$ moment because $\phi,1\in\Phi_t$, and $k_t\psi=E_t(\phi-\pi_t\phi)\in\Psi_{t-1}$ by the recursive $\Psi_t$ condition. [A1, F1, F3, F4, F5, F6, F7, given, algebra]

2.1 For the mutation part, condition on the selected parent paths $\check X_{t-1}^{1:N}$ and set $m_i=k_t\psi(\check X_{t-1}^i)$. Under the product kernel in [F2], $D_{i,N}=\psi(X_t^i)-m_i$ are independent and centered. Their row variance is
$$s_N^2=\frac1N\sum_{i=1}^N\operatorname{Var}_{k_t(\check X_{t-1}^i)}(\psi),$$
which converges in probability to $\sigma^2=\pi_{t-1}(\operatorname{Var}_{k_t}(\psi))$ by [F3], because $0\le\operatorname{Var}_{k_t}(\psi)\le k_t(\psi^2)$ and $\pi_{t-1}(k_t|\psi|^{2+\delta})=\widetilde\pi_t(|\psi|^{2+\delta})<\infty$. When $\sigma^2>0$, normalize the array by $s_N\sqrt N$, where $s_N^2$ is the displayed variance. For every $a>0$, the resulting conditional Lindeberg sum is at most
$$C_\delta a^{-\delta}N^{-\delta/2}s_N^{-(2+\delta)}\,\check\eta_{t-1}^N(k_t|\psi|^{2+\delta}),$$
where $C_\delta$ is a finite constant from $|a-b|^{2+\delta}\le2^{1+\delta}(|a|^{2+\delta}+|b|^{2+\delta})$ and Jensen's inequality. Since $s_N\to\sigma>0$ and [F3] makes the average factor converge in probability to a finite value, this conditional Lindeberg sum tends to zero. [A1, F1, F2, F3, given]

2.2 Along any subsequence, choose a further subsequence on which $s_N\to\sigma$ almost surely. If $\sigma>0$, a further subsequence makes the normalized Lindeberg sums converge almost surely; [F4] gives a standard-normal limit for the normalized row, and Slutsky [F5] with $s_N\to\sigma$ gives the conditional characteristic-function limit $e^{-u^2\sigma^2/2}$. If $\sigma=0$, conditional [F6] gives
$$P\!\left(\left|N^{-1/2}\sum_iD_{i,N}\right|>a\,\middle|\,\check X_{t-1}^{1:N}\right)\le\min(1,s_N^2/a^2)\longrightarrow0$$
for every $a>0$, yielding the same characteristic-function limit with variance zero. The subsequence criterion therefore gives convergence in probability of the conditional characteristic functions along the full sequence. They are bounded by one, so their $L^1$ differences from that limit also tend to zero. [F4, F5, F6, step 2.1, algebra]

2.3 The conditional mean part is
$$P_N=\sqrt N\left(\check\eta_{t-1}^N(k_t\psi)-\pi_{t-1}(k_t\psi)\right),$$
and has the previous selected-population CLT by the hypothesis of the Statement. The total proposal error is $P_N+N^{-1/2}\sum_iD_{i,N}$. Multiplying the conditional characteristic function from step 2.2 by the bounded factor $e^{iuP_N}$ and integrating shows that its limit is the product of the previous Gaussian characteristic function and $e^{-u^2\sigma^2/2}$. Hence the two covariance contributions add, giving $\widetilde V_t(\psi)$. [F1, F2, step 2.2, given]

3.1 For $\phi\in\Psi_t$, apply the mutation result to $\psi=\upsilon_t(\phi-\pi_t\phi)$ using step 1.1 and the preceding selected CLT for $k_t\psi\in\Psi_{t-1}$. By [F3], $\eta_t^N(\upsilon_t)\to\widetilde\pi_t(\upsilon_t)=1$ in probability, and the event of a zero denominator has probability tending to zero. On its complement,
$$\sqrt N\left(\omega_t^N(\phi)-\pi_t(\phi)\right)=\frac{\sqrt N\,\eta_t^N(\upsilon_t(\phi-\pi_t\phi))}{\eta_t^N(\upsilon_t)}.$$
Slutsky [F5] gives the stated limit with covariance $\widetilde V_t(\upsilon_t(\phi-\pi_t\phi))=V_t(\phi)$. The fallback on a zero empirical weight sum changes the ratio only on an event whose probability tends to zero. [F1, F3, F5, step 1.1, step 2.3, algebra] ∎
